items.title: Trump’s Iran dilemma: five options, no clear exit after the midterms
items.summary: Investing.com -- Brent crude has fallen 16.27% in a week to $98.48. The S&P 500 is at 7,407.94, and the VIX has dropped 14.25% on the day. Markets are betting the war’s political pressure is easing, even though the military situation hasn’t changed. (Prices as of Nov 6, 2026, 3:07 PM EST.) Bloomberg Economics’ Fault Lines newsletter argues the pressure is not yet a way out. items.title: European gas tumbles to seal worst week since 2025, snaps five-week rally
items.summary: Investing.com - European wholesale natural gas prices fell sharply on Friday, sliding 3.5% on the day to seal their steepest weekly drop in more than a year and a half, as a relentless retreat across global crude benchmarks and the political fallout from the U.S. midterm elections abruptly dismantled a five-week winning streak.

items.title: Brent posts worst week since April 2020 amid post-midterms hopes for Iran detente
items.summary: Investing.com -- The global oil benchmark on Friday slumped nearly 17% for the week to post its worst weekly performance since late April 2020, as energy market participants assessed the implications of the Democratic midterm election victory on hopes for de-escalation between the U.S. and Iran.

items.title: Procter & Gamble vs. Colgate-Palmolive: Which Dividend Stock Is Safer?
items.summary: Both consumer giants beat earnings, yet their margins are moving in opposite directions as oil prices climb and a cautious U.S. shopper holds back. One dividend carries a thin balance sheet buffer, and retirees need to know which one.

items.title: Colgate-Palmolive Stock Outlook: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish?
items.summary: Colgate-Palmolive has outpaced the broader market over the past year, and analysts remain moderately bullish about the stock’s prospects.

items.title: Coca-Cola Is Up 39% This Year. How Much of That Is Earnings and How Much Is Multiple?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCoca-Cola stock is up 39% this year, and the midterm rally sent it, Procter & Gamble and Colgate-Palmolive toward 52-week highs. Roughly three-quarters of Coca-Cola’s gain came from investors paying a higher multiple, and only about a quarter from higher earnings estimates.

items.title: U.S. midterms fallout in focus; Qualcomm shares slip - what’s moving markets
items.summary: Investing.com - Futures linked to the main U.S. stock indices hover around both sides of the flatline, as investors digest a major Democratic victory in the American midterm elections and begin looking ahead to the release of key employment data later in the week. Chipmakers in the U.S. and Asia retreat amid expectations that Democrats could increase regulatory scrutiny on the artificial intelligence industry, while Qualcomm shares fall on weak smartphone chip demand.

items.title: Asia stocks mixed as chip rout triggers KOSPI trading halt; China outperforms
items.summary: Investing.com-- Asian stocks were mixed on Thursday, as a sharp selloff in semiconductor shares triggered a trading curb in South Korea, offsetting support from a steep decline in oil prices after Democrats’ victories in the U.S. midterm elections.
